classification.difficultyReason: Infer the hemisphere radius from the two heights, use it with the cone height to calculate slant height by Pythagoras, then combine the exposed curved areas and exclude the internal join.

content.prompt:
A hemisphere sits on a cone and two height measurements are given as shown.
Find the surface area of the solid, correct to 1 decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded upper hemisphere joined to a downward-pointing cone. Both height dimensions are outside the solid. The rear joining arc is dashed; the front joining arc and outer silhouette are solid. This composite requires independent geometry review.
spec.mathematics: The hemisphere and cone share radius r. Cone perpendicular height is 10 cm; total height is 15 cm, so r = 5 cm. The illustrative coordinate model uses radius 1 and cone height 2, with joining-ellipse flattening 0.3. Cone silhouette endpoints are derived from tangency to that ellipse.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 10 cm and 15 cm dimensions appear; inferred radius, slant height and surface area are withheld.

answer.worked:
The shared circular face is internal and is excluded.
$$\begin{align*}
r &= 15-10 = 5\text{ cm}\\
l^2 &= 10^2+5^2\\
l &= \sqrt{125}\text{ cm}\\
A &= 2\pi r^2+\pi rl\\
A &= 2\pi(5)^2+\pi(5)\sqrt{125}\\
A &= 50\pi+25\pi\sqrt{5}\\
A &\approx 332.7\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$
